patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Genesys share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Dialpad and Genesys share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Dialpad only if your buying job matches “AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard fr” rather than Genesys's shape. Choose Genesys only if your buying job matches “Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; CX 3 $155; ” rather than Dialpad's shape. Workflow advantage: Dialpad leans business-phone, team-communication; Genesys leans contact-center, customer-messaging. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Genesys share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Dialpad is AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard from $15/user/month annual; Sell and Support are sep; Genesys is Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; CX 3 $155; CX 4 $240..
- Company-size focus: Dialpad (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Genesys (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Dialpad-leaning business-phone, team-communication vs Genesys-leaning contact-center, customer-messaging.
- Researched limits: Dialpad — Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Genesys — Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone.

Limitations — Dialpad: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Connect Pro has a 3-user minimum; Enterprise requires 100 users; Genesys: Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone; CX 1 is voice-only; digital channels require CX 2 or digital add-ons.

Poor-fit cases: Dialpad is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price · Genesys is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone · Avoid Dialpad if you actually need Genesys's motion (Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; C)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
